profile.headline: Software Engineer at Meta
profile.summary: Expertise in the design and development of flash-based storage stack  from firmware/microcode to file systems with strong backgrounds in embedded operating systems. Lots of hands-on experiences developing and debugging embedded systems.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Platform software for Meta's in-house AI accelerator chip (GPU)
DRAM-SSD hybrid cache core engine (cachelib) used by Meta infrastructure services

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
* Linux kernel development for FlashArray product - block layer and NVMe/SCSI host driver
* NVMeF/RoCEv2 and NVMeF/FC stack development
* RDMA over NTB driver development
* Intel Skylake architectural bug (Mesh/PCIe/NTB related CATERR propagation) investigation and debugging

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Worked on Android kernel and vendor HAL

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer, Founding Member
positions.description:
* Developed a firmware for many-core (over 15) 4TB NVMe SSD based on 3D MLC flash memory
- Redesigned and developed the backend (FTL) schemes such as address mapping, garbage collection, write throttling, wear leveling, power-loss protection, and NAND co-processor interface.
* Led a team developing differentiated storage solutions and served as a main developer.
- Developed a new NAND storage solution called eMMCplus consisting of a Linux block layer software and a eMMC device firmware implementing a newly devised protocol which enables to effectively partition computation- and/or memory-bound FTL tasks between devices and hosts.
- Developed a full set of the development supporting toolkit including debugfs-like tool for analyzing host-FTL image data, ftrace- and blktrace-based framework for tracing and analysis, execution time Gantt-chart visualizer, storage access pattern analysis scripts, and monkeyrunner-based test automator for Android.

positions.title: Senior Engineer
positions.description:
* Developed FTL based on the event-driven architecture for commercial SATA-2 SSDs (inc. world-first MLC SSD).
- Devised/applied the in-block logging technique and a technique for parallelizing the garbage collection and the wear leveling operations.
- Devised and applied a multi-tasking emulation technique to (monolithic) FTL to bound the response times of IOs
- Developed a common software platform consisting of a real-time operating systems and a multi-core communications middleware (newly developed) and applied it to Samsung’s first multi-core SSD.
* Developed RawSSD which exposes NAND-like native interface and developed iSCSI-based Object-SSD (SCSI OSD command set) on Linux (in collaboration with University)
* Devised the in-storage processing (ISP) concept and performed the feasibility study by applying the concept to PostgreSQL acceleration (in collaboration with University)
